2026-09-22.name: Steve Cantrell
2026-09-22.title: A Moduli Space of Quasi-morphisms on Subshifts of Finite Type
2026-09-22.abstract: We introduce and discuss a moduli space of functions (quasi-morphisms) on subshifts of finite type which we equip with a metric that measures the 'distortion' required to move from one function to another. We’ll discuss the fundamental properties of this space and explain how pressure curves form geodesics (locally length minimising paths) connecting quasi-morphisms.

2026-09-29.name: Antti Käenmäki
2026-09-29.title: Exponential separation of self-conformal systems
2026-09-29.abstract: Exponential separation rules out a dimension drop for planar self-conformal sets and measures, by a recent theorem of Feng and Rapaport, but it is hard to verify for a concrete non-linear system. Bárány, Kolossváry, and Troscheit made it checkable on the real line through a dual iterated function system; the quantity their condition separates is the pre-Schwarzian derivative. I will explain how this carries the construction to the plane and one level higher, to the Schwarzian, and how the resulting conditions are C^2-open and dense, making the absence of a dimension drop C^2-generic in the plane.

2026-10-06.name: Jonathan Fraser
2026-10-06.title: Quantitative flatness and obstructions in Fourier analysis
2026-10-06.abstract: If a measure in Euclidean space has ‘flat parts’, for example, anisotropic cuboids which contain a lot of mass, then this is an ‘enemy’ of Fourier decay.  I will explore this idea by trying to derive explicit upper bounds for the Fourier dimension of a measure in terms of quantitative notions of flatness. I will also discuss several applications of these ideas.

2026-10-13.name: Markus Myllyoja
2026-10-13.title: Visible parts and projections of the affine fractal percolation
2026-10-13.abstract: In this talk I will discuss the visible parts and orthogonal projections of the affine fractal percolation. For all directions apart from the y-axis, typical visible parts and orthogonal projections behave in a manner one might expect, and their dimension equals the minimum of one and dimension of the affine percolation. For the non-expectional case of the y-axis, the visible part exhibits more complicated behaviour and I will discuss its Hausdorff and box dimensions. During the talk, I may also mention that the projection contains an interval to all directions except the y-axis provided that the dimension of the percolation is larger than one. Based on joint work with Eeva Kuure and Aleksi Pyörälä.

2026-10-20.name: Firdavs Rahkmonov
2026-10-20.title: Majorization and additive tuples in $\mathbb{Z}_2^n$
2026-10-20.abstract: Majorization provides a way to compare how “spread out” the entries of two vectors are. It has important applications in additive combinatorics, with classical results by Hardy, Littlewood and Pólya for the integers and by Lev for cyclic groups of prime order. In this talk, I will establish a powerful majorization theorem for the hypercube $\mathbb{Z}_2^n$ and explain the compression method behind its proof. As an application, we determine the maximum number of solutions to $a_1+\cdots+a_k=0$, where $a_i\in A_i$ and $A_1,\ldots,A_k$ are subsets of the hypercube with prescribed sizes. We also establish the corresponding minimum and characterize all extremal sets when these sets are identical and $k$ is odd. For $k=3$, this counts Schur triples, and we recover a theorem of Samotij and Sudakov. Finally, I will discuss a related convexity inequality and an analogue of Pollard’s theorem for the hypercube that strengthens and extends a result of Bollobás and Leader. Based on joint work with Sophie Huczynska and Chi Hoi Yip.
